Each ten-state component has characteristic polynomial (x+1)(x^4-x^3-1)(x^5+x^3+x+1)=x^10-x^6-2x^4-2x^3-x^2-2x-1. Consequently R1=R3=1, R2=1+4[4|n], and R4=R2+2b_n where b_n=tr(B^n), and primitive four-cycle orbits equal (R4-R2)/4=b_n/2. The all-n theorem rests on complete finite-state transfer and Perron proof; finite brute force is corroboration, not infinity proof.
